question: What is the main public health goal of achieving high herd immunity within a community?

options.A: To guarantee lifelong immunity without booster doses
options.B: To protect vulnerable individuals who cannot receive vaccines
options.C: To reduce the financial cost of hospital admissions
options.D: To completely eliminate all known chronic illnesses

explanation: When most of the population is vaccinated, it creates a protective barrier that stops infectious agents from reaching people who are too young or sick to get vaccinated. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T61#GNS214_U1_T61_h1)

question: Why is immunization considered a fundamental component of Primary Health Care?

options.A: It is delivered exclusively inside major tertiary teaching hospitals
options.B: It replaces the need for proper sanitation and clean drinking water
options.C: It provides affordable, community-based disease prevention for all
options.D: It focuses on treating advanced stages of communicable diseases

explanation: Primary Health Care aims to bring essential health services as close as possible to where people live, making preventive measures like vaccines easily accessible. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T61#GNS214_U1_T61_h1)

question: How does an infant acquire natural passive immunity from their mother?

options.A: Through receiving routine childhood routine immunizations
options.B: By producing antibodies after surviving a childhood illness
options.C: By inheriting active immune memory cells during conception
options.D: Through the transfer of maternal antibodies via breast milk

explanation: Maternal antibodies pass to the baby across the placenta and through breast milk, giving the newborn temporary protection against common infections. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T61#GNS214_U1_T61_h2)

question: What is the primary clinical advantage of active immunity over passive immunity?

options.A: Active immunity does not require exposure to any antigens
options.B: Active immunity can be easily transferred through blood transfusions
options.C: Active immunity lasts much longer due to immunological memory
options.D: Active immunity provides immediate protection within minutes

explanation: When the body creates its own antibodies and memory cells during active immunity, it remembers the germ and protects against future exposures for years. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T61#GNS214_U1_T61_h2)

question: Which vaccines are routinely scheduled to be given immediately at birth in Nigeria?

options.A: BCG, OPV zero, and Hepatitis B zero
options.B: Pentavalent first dose and Rotavirus vaccine
options.C: Measles, Yellow fever, and Meningitis vaccines
options.D: Inactivated Polio Vaccine and PCV first dose

explanation: At birth, newborns receive BCG for tuberculosis, OPV 0 for polio, and the birth dose of Hepatitis B to prevent early mother-to-child transmission. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T61#GNS214_U1_T61_h3)

question: A mother brings her healthy 14-week-old infant to the primary health clinic. Which group of vaccines is due for this visit?

options.A: BCG, OPV zero, and Hepatitis B birth dose
options.B: Measles first dose and Yellow Fever vaccine
options.C: Rotavirus first dose and Pentavalent first dose
options.D: Pentavalent third dose, OPV 3, IPV, and PCV 3

explanation: At 14 weeks, infants receive the third doses of Pentavalent, OPV, and PCV, along with the first dose of Inactivated Polio Vaccine (IPV). [learn more](GNS214_U1_T61#GNS214_U1_T61_h3)

question: What is the primary clinical complication caused by the poliovirus?

options.A: Irreversible muscle paralysis in the limbs
options.B: High fever accompanied by a widespread skin rash
options.D: Severe chronic diarrhea and rapid dehydration

explanation: Poliovirus attacks the nervous system, which can lead to total, permanent paralysis, most commonly affecting the legs. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T61#GNS214_U1_T61_h4)

question: Which of the following describes the main characteristic feature of pertussis infection?

options.A: Persistent watery diarrhea lasting several weeks
options.C: Yellow discoloration of the skin and eyes
options.D: Stiff jaw muscles and painful body spasms

explanation: Pertussis, commonly known as whooping cough, is famous for causing severe, hacking cough fits that end with a high-pitched whooping sound. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T61#GNS214_U1_T61_h4)

question: What is the safe temperature range for storing routine vaccines like Pentavalent and PCV in a clinic refrigerator?
explanation: Routine diluents and liquid vaccines like Pentavalent and PCV must be kept cool between two and eight degrees Celsius and never frozen. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T61#GNS214_U1_T61_h5)

question: What is the primary purpose of a Vaccine Vial Monitor (VVM) attached to a vaccine container?

options.A: To indicate if the vaccine has been exposed to damaging heat
options.B: To detect if the vaccine has accidentally been frozen solid
options.C: To measure the exact expiry date set by the factory
options.D: To show the precise number of vaccine doses remaining inside

explanation: The VVM changes color progressively when exposed to heat over time, giving nurses a visual warning that the vaccine potency may be compromised. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T61#GNS214_U1_T61_h5)

question: Which injection route is standard for administering the Bacillus Calmette-Guérin (BCG) vaccine to a newborn?

options.A: Deep intravenous bolus injection into a peripheral vein
options.B: Intramuscular injection into the thigh muscle
options.C: Intradermal injection to create a shallow skin wheal
options.D: Subcutaneous injection into the fatty arm tissue

explanation: BCG is given intradermally into the superficial layers of the skin, typically on the upper arm, producing a characteristic small raised bleb. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T61#GNS214_U1_T61_h6)

question: Why are auto-disable syringes specifically used during routine immunization campaigns?

options.A: They lock automatically after one use to prevent accidental reuse
options.B: They allow nurses to draw medication much faster than regular needles
options.C: They can be safely disposed of in regular household waste bins
options.D: They reduce the physical pain of the injection for crying infants

explanation: Auto-disable syringes are designed to render themselves unserviceable after a single injection, stopping the spread of infections from reused equipment. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T61#GNS214_U1_T61_h6)

question: What is the immediate drug of choice for managing severe anaphylactic shock following a vaccination?
explanation: Epinephrine is the life-saving treatment for anaphylaxis because it quickly constricts blood vessels, relaxes airway passages, and raises dropping blood pressure. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T61#GNS214_U1_T61_h7)

question: Which event is classified as an immunization error-related adverse event?

options.A: A child developing a mild fever due to an immune response
options.B: A mild allergic rash caused by an egg protein allergy
options.C: An abscess forming due to unsterile injection techniques
options.D: A baby catching an unrelated malaria infection the next day

explanation: Immunization errors happen due to mistakes in handling, preparation, or administration, such as introducing bacteria through poor aseptic technique. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T61#GNS214_U1_T61_h7)

question: How should a nurse best approach a caregiver who expresses fear and hesitation about routine childhood vaccines?

options.A: Scold the parent for ignoring professional medical advice
options.B: Report the parent to local law enforcement authorities
options.C: Listen respectfully and provide clear, reassuring education
options.D: Ignore their concerns and administer the vaccines anyway

explanation: Building trust through empathetic listening and clear, respectful communication is the most effective way to address vaccine hesitancy and correct rumors. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T61#GNS214_U1_T61_h8)

question: What is the most effective way to improve community participation in rural immunization drives?

options.A: Relying solely on written posters placed inside clinic walls
options.B: Stopping all routine clinic visits to focus only on mass rallies
options.C: Engaging local community and religious leaders as advocates
options.D: Punishing parents who fail to bring their babies on time

explanation: Working with respected community and religious leaders helps build local trust and encourages families to accept and support immunization programs. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T61#GNS214_U1_T61_h8)
